Next, we will extend our analysis to all positive rationals with a constant added to the bound. ▶ Theorem 4. Let α be an unknown rational number in (0, ∞). The algorithm Compressed Stern-Brocot Tree Search outputs α with no more than 2.5849 log2 n + 2 queries of the form “β ≤ α” where n is the greater of the numerator and the denominator of α. For our first query, we determine whether α > 1, α < 1, or α = 1. For α = 1, we will conclude our search in a single query. For α < 1, the search is now over the range (0, 1), starting from 1/1, and Theorem 1 applies. This gives a bound of 2.5849 log2 n + 1 queries. For α > 1, the algorithm then performs a search in the range (1, ∞). This is the equivalent to performing a search for 1/α ∈ (0, 1). In our algorithm, we have already started our search going to the right with 1/1. Thus, Theorem 1 will not directly apply since we are not starting our search from 1/1 but rather continuing the exponential search from 0/1 (and inversely to the left from 1/0 when searching for 1/α).
